title: Credential split by a literal LF or CRLF in plain text
summary: A SendGrid-shaped key in plain text (a note, an email body, a log) is broken by a literal line feed or a carriage return plus line feed, with no construct that joins the lines.
rationale: Nothing rebuilds the value: the text holds two fragments and a separator, which is not the documented key grammar (fixed 69 characters, no separators). It is also a partial leak of a key-shaped value. The ambiguity: stripping whitespace to repair the key would be a global rewrite that turns arbitrary wrapped prose into a credential, and ignoring it may leave a half key in clear text.

expectation.rationale: Unresolved. The provider documents the key as always 69 characters, which the separator-bearing text cannot satisfy, so the text is not a documented key. No source says whether fragments of one must be protected. Candidate outcomes: must-flag the fragments or must-not-flag the joined text. A maintainer decision with a non-author reviewer would settle it. No assertable fixture. Synthetic, never issued: every value in the fixtures is built from the words SYNTHETIC and EXAMPLE, so none can authenticate.

sources.supports: SendGrid API keys are always 69 characters long.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
